Using \(s=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\), \(q=\sum_{i<j}\alpha_i\alpha_j\), the rational function is

\[
r_{s,q}(\lambda)=
\frac{\lambda^3-s\lambda^2+q\lambda-8}
{\lambda^3+s\lambda^2+q\lambda+8},
\qquad s\le {46\over5}.
\]

Its stationary points on \((0,\infty)\) satisfy

\[
s\lambda^4+(24-sq)\lambda^2+8q=0.
\]

The active sets are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{range of }\gamma & \mathcal A_\gamma\\ \hline
(3,\gamma_1) & \{\xi_1,\gamma_1,8\}\\
(\gamma_1,\gamma_2) & \{\xi(\gamma),\gamma,8\}\\
(\gamma_2,\gamma_3) & \{\gamma,8\}\\
(\gamma_3,7) & \{2,8\}.
\end{array}
\]

At the transition points:

\[
\mathcal A_{\gamma_1}=\{\xi_1,\gamma_1,8\},\qquad
\mathcal A_{\gamma_2}=\{\xi(\gamma_2),\gamma_2,8\},\qquad
\mathcal A_{\gamma_3}=\{2,\gamma_3,8\}.
\]

The sum constraint is inactive for \(\gamma<\gamma_2\), and becomes active exactly at \(\gamma_2\). For \(\gamma>\gamma_2\), \(s=46/5\). The minimizing shifts remain positive because the numerator cubic has three positive zeros throughout: initially one is exactly \(2\), and thereafter the zeros move continuously without crossing \(0\).

The exact transition values are:

\[
\gamma_1=\operatorname{root}_{(3,4)}(f_1),
\]

where

\[
\begin{aligned}
f_1(x)=\;&16x^{12}-16x^{11}-8x^{10}-1008x^9+1529x^8-767x^7\\
&+256x^6+16192x^5-28576x^4+16368x^3\\
&-2048x^2-1024x+256.
\end{aligned}
\]

Also

\[
\gamma_2=\operatorname{root}_{(5,11/2)}(f_2),
\]

where \(f_2\) is the resultant polynomial obtained from the endpoint alternation \(r(\gamma)=-r(8)\), the low stationary equation, and \(r(\xi)=r(8)\), with \(s=46/5\).

Finally,

\[
\gamma_3=\operatorname{root}_{(11/2,6)}(f_3),
\]

where

\[
f_3(x)=700x^6+17250x^5-244917x^4+906848x^3
-1333688x^2+775520x-149200.
\]

Numerically,

\[
\boxed{(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)
=(3.7787240783,\;5.2442756394,\;5.8746294511)}.
\]
